examples.question_text: Rewrite $5a^{-4}b^{-2}$ with positive indices. Assume all variables are non-zero.
examples.solution_text:
Only the factors with negative indices move to the denominator; the coefficient stays.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5a^{-4}b^{-2}\\&=5\times\frac{1}{a^{4}}\times\frac{1}{b^{2}}\\&=\frac{5}{a^{4}b^{2}}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Rewrite $6r^{5}s^{-4}$ with positive indices. Assume all variables are non-zero.
examples.solution_text:
The $r^{5}$ already has a positive index, so it stays in the numerator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}6r^{5}s^{-4}\\&=6r^{5}\times\frac{1}{s^{4}}\\&=\frac{6r^{5}}{s^{4}}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Rewrite $\frac{8}{p^{-3}q^{2}}$ with positive indices. Assume all variables are non-zero.
examples.solution_text:
Only $p^{-3}$ moves up; $q^{2}$ stays in the denominator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{8}{p^{-3}q^{2}}\\&=\frac{8}{q^{2}}\div\frac{1}{p^{3}}\\&=\frac{8}{q^{2}}\times p^{3}\\&=\frac{8p^{3}}{q^{2}}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Write $\frac{5r^{2}t^{3}}{12s^{4}}$ as a single term whose only fraction is its coefficient, using a negative index where needed. Assume all variables are non-zero.

examples.solution_text:
The index applies only to $z$, so the coefficient $-5$ stays.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-5z^{-4}\\&=-5\times\frac{1}{z^{4}}\\&=-\frac{5}{z^{4}}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Rewrite each expression with positive indices and no brackets. Assume all variables are non-zero.
(a) $(5m)^{-2}$
(b) $r(st)^{-2}$
(c) $(-2uv)^{-3}$
examples.solution_text:
The reciprocal applies to the whole bracketed base. Each factor inside the brackets receives the positive power.
(a)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(5m)^{-2}\\&=\frac{1}{(5m)^{2}}\\&=\frac{1}{5^{2}m^{2}}\\&=\frac{1}{25m^{2}}\end{aligned}$
(b)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}r(st)^{-2}\\&=r\times\frac{1}{(st)^{2}}\\&=\frac{r}{s^{2}t^{2}}\end{aligned}$
(c)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(-2uv)^{-3}\\&=\frac{1}{(-2uv)^{3}}\\&=\frac{1}{(-2)^{3}u^{3}v^{3}}\\&=-\frac{1}{8u^{3}v^{3}}\end{aligned}$

The $7$ has no negative index, so it stays in the denominator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{r^{-4}}{7}\\&=\frac{1}{r^{4}}\div7\\&=\frac{1}{7r^{4}}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Rewrite $\frac{7a^{3}c^{-2}}{8b^{-4}d}$ with positive indices. Assume all variables are non-zero.
examples.solution_text:
The $c^{-2}$ moves down and the $b^{-4}$ moves up. All other factors stay.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{7a^{3}c^{-2}}{8b^{-4}d}\\&=\frac{7a^{3}}{8d}\times\frac{1}{c^{2}}\div\frac{1}{b^{4}}\\&=\frac{7a^{3}}{8dc^{2}}\times b^{4}\\&=\frac{7a^{3}b^{4}}{8c^{2}d}\end{aligned}$
